title: 光子晶片光開關矩陣
summary: 從開關拓撲、損失串接與可觀測性拆成 4 階段、24 項可保存的工程作業；包含物理模型、算例、可區分失效的量測與驗收證據。
summaryEn: Four stages and 24 saveable work packages investigate switch topology, cascaded loss and observability, including physical models, a worked example, discriminating measurements and acceptance evidence.
scope: 公開原理的概念設計與資料判讀課，非供應商配方或可直接投產的操作程序。算例全部是教學假設；真正驗收須使用適用版本、合格設備與實測參數。代表照片、示意圖與影片不宣稱為每步製造實拍。
scopeEn: Conceptual design and data interpretation from public principles, not a vendor recipe or production-ready procedure. All worked inputs are educational assumptions. Real acceptance requires the applicable revision, qualified equipment and measured parameters. Representative media are not claimed as footage of every operation.

stages.title: 路由與單元
stages.description: 以三個技術單元完成「路由與單元」的模型與驗證，六項作業各自留存交付物。
stages.descriptionEn: Three technical units address Routes and units through six separately saved modeling and verification work packages.

steps.title: 非阻塞定義：模型與設計
steps.objective: 以「非阻塞定義」建立可檢驗的物理模型，交付可重算且列明邊界的工程紀錄。
steps.objectiveEn: Build a falsifiable physical model for nonblocking definitions, with reproducible calculations and stated boundaries.
steps.instruction: 先以師傅示意確認「非阻塞定義」的輸入、輸出與座標，再在學徒工作台完成對應元件或資料流的排列。嚴格非阻塞與可重排非阻塞不同；後者可能需改變既有連線。 用本單元的變數畫出至少兩種設計狀態，說明它們在「用四埠圖列兩種需求，檢查新連線是否迫使舊路由搬移。」的驗證中應有何差異；把待量測參數另列，不以動畫位置當成實際公差。
steps.instructionEn: Use the mentor view to identify the inputs, outputs and coordinates for nonblocking definitions, then arrange the corresponding components or data flow in the apprentice workspace. Strictly nonblocking and rearrangeably nonblocking differ; the latter may need existing connections changed. Draw at least two design states using this unit's variables and predict how the following verification distinguishes them: Use a four-port graph to test whether a new connection forces an existing route to move. List unmeasured parameters separately; animation positions are not manufacturing tolerances.
steps.observation: 用四埠圖列兩種需求，檢查新連線是否迫使舊路由搬移。
steps.observationEn: Use a four-port graph to test whether a new connection forces an existing route to move.
steps.failure: 須排除的錯誤假說：可重排非阻塞表示永不需要改變舊路由。 若觀察不支持預測，先核對基準與單位，再依本步判別量測定位原因；不能只調參到曲線相合。
steps.failureEn: Incorrect hypothesis to reject: Rearrangeably nonblocking means old routes never change. If observations disagree, first check references and units, then use this step's discriminating measurement; do not simply tune parameters until curves agree.
steps.check: 提交非阻塞定義的兩狀態模型、變數表，以及能由「用四埠圖列兩種需求，檢查新連線是否迫使舊路由搬移。」反駁模型的預測。
steps.checkEn: Submit two model states and a variable table for nonblocking definitions, plus a falsifiable prediction using: Use a four-port graph to test whether a new connection forces an existing route to move.

knowledge.title: 量化模型與適用邊界
knowledge.text: ILroute=ΣILi；可達性與光功率裕度必須同時成立。 假設被動損失、無相干反射與增益；數字是教學工作負載。

quiz.question: 要審查「非阻塞定義」，哪項主張或驗證方法有根據？
quiz.questionEn: Which claim or verification is justified when reviewing nonblocking definitions?
options: 嚴格非阻塞與可重排非阻塞不同；後者可能需改變既有連線。
可重排非阻塞表示永不需要改變舊路由。
最短幾何路徑一定最低光損。
optionsEn: Strictly nonblocking and rearrangeably nonblocking differ; the latter may need existing connections changed.
Rearrangeably nonblocking means old routes never change.
The shortest geometric route always has the least loss.
quiz.explanation: 嚴格非阻塞與可重排非阻塞不同；後者可能需改變既有連線。 用四埠圖列兩種需求，檢查新連線是否迫使舊路由搬移。
quiz.explanationEn: Strictly nonblocking and rearrangeably nonblocking differ; the latter may need existing connections changed. Use a four-port graph to test whether a new connection forces an existing route to move.

steps.title: 非阻塞定義：量測與判別

steps.instructionEn: Retain the previous model and test whether it explains the observations. Use a four-port graph to test whether a new connection forces an existing route to move. Record raw quantities, units, reference conditions and repeatability. Use supporting and falsifying evidence to compare "Strictly nonblocking and rearrangeably nonblocking differ; the latter may need existing connections changed." against the incorrect hypothesis "The shortest geometric route always has the least loss."; decide whether to accept, repeat or revise the model.

steps.check: 提交非阻塞定義的量測判別表：用四埠圖列兩種需求，檢查新連線是否迫使舊路由搬移。 附上基準、重複性或不確定度，及不能由本資料判定的結論。

steps.objective: 以「級聯損失」區分機制並作出有證據的驗收決定，交付可重算且列明邊界的工程紀錄。
steps.objectiveEn: Discriminate mechanisms and make an evidence-based acceptance decision for cascaded loss, with reproducible calculations and stated boundaries.
steps.instruction: 保留上一作業的模型，現在檢驗它是否足以解釋觀察。按算例比較跳數與損失，保存每元件損失來源。 記錄原始量、單位、基準與重複量測差異；以支持及否定各一項證據比較「多級路由的插損以 dB 加總，短路徑未必有最少交叉或最低損失。」與錯誤假說「可重排非阻塞表示永不需要改變舊路由。」，最後提出放行、重測或修模決定。 假設一路經 6 個開關各 0.4 dB、4 個交叉各 0.05 dB、波導共 0.6 dB，總損失=3.2 dB；1 mW 輸入輸出約 0.479 mW。
steps.instructionEn: Retain the previous model and test whether it explains the observations. Compare hop count and loss in the example and retain per-element sources. Record raw quantities, units, reference conditions and repeatability. Use supporting and falsifying evidence to compare "Route losses add in dB; the shortest geometric route need not have fewest crossings or lowest loss." against the incorrect hypothesis "Rearrangeably nonblocking means old routes never change."; decide whether to accept, repeat or revise the model. Assume six switches at 0.4 dB each, four crossings at 0.05 dB each and 0.6 dB routing loss. Total loss is 3.2 dB; 1 mW input gives about 0.479 mW.
steps.observation: 按算例比較跳數與損失，保存每元件損失來源。
steps.observationEn: Compare hop count and loss in the example and retain per-element sources.
steps.failure: 須排除的錯誤假說：可重排非阻塞表示永不需要改變舊路由。 若觀察不支持預測，先核對基準與單位，再依本步判別量測定位原因；不能只調參到曲線相合。
steps.failureEn: Incorrect hypothesis to reject: Rearrangeably nonblocking means old routes never change. If observations disagree, first check references and units, then use this step's discriminating measurement; do not simply tune parameters until curves agree.
steps.check: 提交級聯損失的量測判別表：按算例比較跳數與損失，保存每元件損失來源。 附上基準、重複性或不確定度，及不能由本資料判定的結論。
steps.checkEn: Submit a measurement-discrimination table for cascaded loss: Compare hop count and loss in the example and retain per-element sources. Include the reference, repeatability or uncertainty, and conclusions the data cannot support.
